items.title: Devils beat Maple Leafs as Hellebuyck posts shutout
items.body: Connor Hellebuyck made 23 saves for his first shutout with New Jersey as the Devils blanked the Toronto Maple Leafs 4-0 on Sunday night. Timo Meier scored twice for New Jersey (13-5-0), which has won nine of its last 10 games. Nico Hischier, with a goal and an assist, and Connor Brown, into an empty net, provided the rest of the offence. Jack Hughes and Jesper Bratt chipped in two assists each. Acquired from the Winnipeg Jets last month, Hellebuyck became the first goaltender in franchise history to win each of his first five games with the club. Anthony Stolarz stopped 25 shots for Toronto (8-9-2). The Maple Leafs have lost three straight, and five of their last six in regulation. Meier gave his team a 1-0 lead at 8:28 of the second period when he was left alone in front after a faceoff in the offensive zone. The Devils winger doubled the visitors' advantage at 12:44 when a Hughes shot deflected off Meier and past Stolarz. Hischier made it 3-0 on a power play at 9:49 of the third before Brown iced it into the empty net. The Hockey Hall of Fame's class of 2026 was honoured before puck drop. Carey Price, Patrice Bergeron, Pekka Rinne, Keith Tkachuk and Cindy Curley are set to be enshrined in the player category Monday. Brian Burke will go in as a builder. Jack Roslovic was a late scratch with a lower-body injury despite taking part in warm-ups, while fellow forward Colton Sissons didn't return after the second with the same designation. items.title: Scheifele’s winner with 1.6 seconds remaining lifts Jets over Lightning
items.body: Mark Scheifele scored with 1.6 seconds remaining in the third period to lead the Winnipeg Jets to a 4-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Sunday. With the period winding down and the Jets on a 5-on-3 power play, Scheifele converted a pass from Cole Perfetti before firing home a slapshot to seal the win at Canada Life Centre. "(Perfetti) and Gabe (Vilardi) getting dirty in the corner and making a great play," Scheifele said of his goal after the win. "That was an unbelievable pass and you don't quit until the buzzer, and that was exactly that." Scheifele said that he "had no idea" how much time was left on the clock when he secured the pass from Perfetti, but added that he "wasn't going to waste (his) time looking at the clock" when the puck came out. Tampa Bay tied the game 3-3 with a pair of Pontus Holmberg goals 26 seconds apart late in the third period. "It's not very fun," Scheifele said of the swing on the scoreboard. "It's definitely not how we wanted to win that game, but kudos to them. ... That's a good hockey team right there. They don't quit. Even on a back-to-back, being down three, they kept making plays, they kept doing good things. Morgan Barron, Brayden Yager and Perfetti also scored for Winnipeg (7-8-3), which extended its win streak to three games after dropping its previous nine. Rookie Viggo Bjorck tallied two assists. Yager's tally marked his first NHL goal in his sixth game with the Jets. "That was really cool," the 21-year-old said post-game. items.summary: The Los Angeles Kings have assigned winger Martin Chromiak to AHL Ontario.
items.body: Register Login Kings Assign Martin Chromiak To AHL By Brian La Rose | at November 8, 2026 8:26 pm With the Kings activating Alex Turcotte off injured reserve yesterday, winger Martin Chromiak found himself out of the lineup. Now, he’s off the roster altogether, as the team announced ( Twitter link ) that they’ve returned Chromiak to AHL Ontario. The 24-year-old was brought up about a week and a half ago but didn’t see much action, getting into just two games. That said, they were Chromiak’s first two appearances at the NHL level. He was held off the scoresheet while recording three shots on goal and two hits in a little over 13 minutes per night of ice time. A 2020 fifth-round pick, Chromiak had gotten off to a hot start with the Reign to earn this short-lived promotion. Prior to the recall, he had collected six goals and two assists in nine games. He basically picked up where he left off a year ago, when he had 28 goals and 28 assists in 71 outings with Ontario, a performance that earned him a one-year, two-way deal worth $850K in the NHL and $200K in guaranteed money this offseason. With the Kings operating very tight to the cap ceiling this season, Chromiak’s assignment now gives them enough cap space to be able to bring someone up should more injuries arise. In the meantime, they now have one open roster spot, with veterans Mats Zuccarello and Kevin Fiala working their way towards a return to the lineup. Accordingly, one more spot will need to be opened up when both wingers are able to return.

items.title: Devils’ Anthony Mantha to ‘miss some time’ with throat injury
items.summary: The Devils went with 11 forwards and 7 defensemen for their game in Toronto on Sunday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources New Jersey Devils forward Anthony Mantha will “miss some time” with a throat injury he sustained in the team’s 5-4 overtime win over the New York Islanders on Saturday, according to head coach Sheldon Keefe. Mantha, 32, took the stick of Islanders defenseman Adam Pelech to his throat area midway through the third period of Saturday’s game on Long Island. Pelech was assessed a two-minute minor penalty for high-sticking on the play; Mantha left the game shortly thereafter and did not return. The Devils went with 11 forwards and seven defensemen without Mantha in their lineup for Sunday’s game against the Toronto Maple Leafs at Scotiabank Arena. The Devils signed Mantha to a two-year contract as an unrestricted free agent on July 15. The 6’5″ winger has five goals and 10 points in 17 games with the Devils this season; he’s signed through 2028 at a $4.75 million annual cap hit. Mantha earned his contract in New Jersey after a career-best 33-goal, 64-point season with the Pittsburgh Penguins in 2025-26. The Longueuil, Que. product has now played for six NHL teams in his 605-game career. The Detroit Red Wings originally selected Mantha in the first round (No. 20 overall) of the 2013 NHL Draft. The former Val d’Or Foreurs standout debuted with the Red Wings in the 2015-16 season and ultimately surpassed the 20-goal mark twice over parts of six seasons in Detroit before being traded to the Washington Capitals in 2021. items.title: Panthers Recall Jack Devine
items.summary: The Florida Panthers have recalled winger Jack Devine from AHL Charlotte.
items.body: Register Login Panthers Recall Jack Devine By Brian La Rose | at November 8, 2026 6:46 pm Prior to their game against Boston this afternoon, the Panthers added some extra depth to their forward group. The team announced that they’ve recalled winger Jack Devine from AHL Charlotte. The 23-year-old was a seventh-round pick back in 2021, going 221st overall in 2022 and has clearly outperformed that draft selection. After a strong four seasons at the University of Denver (including tallying 56 and 57 points in his final two years), Devine turned pro last season, playing predominantly with the Checkers. In 63 games with them in 2025-26, Devine had a good rookie campaign, tallying 18 goals and 25 assists. He had a brief two-week stint with Florida early on in the year, getting into six games with the Panthers although he was held off the scoresheet. This season, Devine got off to an impressive start with Charlotte, notching nine goals and three assists through 11 appearances. Devine’s recall comes on the heels of the injury that Sandis Vilmanis sustained on Saturday. Head coach Paul Maurice indicated that while they’ve had a doctor look at the youngster already, they probably won’t get a full assessment of the injury until they return home. Florida has one game left on its road trip on Tuesday in Columbus so it will be a few more days before the severity of the injury to Vilmanis is known. In the short term, Devine will serve as the extra forward while they get a better sense of how long Vilmanis will be out for. Depending on the severity of the injury, Florida could reassess who they want in the reserve role from there. The Panthers had an open roster spot so no corresponding move needed to be made to bring Devine up.

Going from an ECHLer to a two-time Stanley Cup champion and legitimate top-six threat, Gourde returned to Tampa after 3 1/2 years with the Kraken. A beloved veteran no longer expected to drive the same amount of offense, he suited up for all 82 games last year recording 28 points. It was the fourth time the spark plug surpassed the 100-hit mark, landing 115. Facing multiple first round playoff exits, the Lightning made an effort to strengthen their middle-six along with adding a star in John Carlson . Their current 11-3-2 record speaks to the improvements made during the offseason. During Gourde’s absence the sudden uncertainty surrounding Nikita Kucherov dropped out of nowhere, but with whatever is in store with that situation, for now the Bolts boast one of the strongest top-nine forward groups in the league.

items.title: Report: Blackhawks not making coaching change amid slump
items.body: It appears the Chicago Blackhawks are staying the course amid some choppy waters. Jeff Blashill will remain as Blackhawks' head coach as the team has opted not to make a coaching change, The Athletic 's Scott Powers reported on Sunday. The Blackhawks, in a rebuild for the better part of a decade, were intending this to be a season in which they turned a corner. Instead, they've started the year 4-13-1 — better only than the lowly Vancouver Canucks in the Western Conference. Things hit a low point with a 9-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes on Saturday night. The Blackhawks were off Sunday and don't play again until Thursday, which led many to wonder whether regime change is imminent. Instead, it appears general manager Kyle Davidson is giving Blashill some more time to right the ship. The former Detroit Red Wings coach was hired by Chicago ahead of the 2025-26 season. The Blackhawks missed the playoffs for the sixth consecutive season with a 29-39-14 record.

items.title: Hertl scores pair, Golden Knights beat Sabres for third win in a row
items.body: BUFFALO, N.Y. — Tomas Hertl scored two goals and the Vegas Golden Knights won their third straight game, 4-1 over the Buffalo Sabres on Sunday. Hertl scored both of his goals in the third period to help put the game away for the Golden Knights, who finished their road trip 3-0-1. Jack Eichel and Mitch Marner also scored for Vegas while Adin Hill made 27 saves. Beck Malenstyn scored and Colten Ellis made 21 saves for Buffalo, which has lost two of its last three games. Marner opened the scoring with a short-handed goal at 12:17 of the second period following a turnover by Tage Thompson. Eichel, who was the Sabres' first-round draft pick in 2015 and traded to Vegas in 2021, made it 2-0 one minute and 26 seconds later with his eighth goal of the season. He has seven goals and three assists in eight games against Buffalo in his career. Malenstyn cut the Vegas lead to 2-1 with his first goal on a goalmouth scrum at 4:26 of the third period, but Hertl made it 3-1 just 1:17 later. Hertl’s second of the game and ninth of the season made it 4-1 at 10:00. Buffalo concludes a four-game homestand against Tampa Bay on Wednesday night. Vegas begins a five-game homestand against Utah on Wednesday night.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images A couple of netminders have hit the wire. On Sunday, the Chicago Blackhawks placed goaltender Arvid Soderblom on waivers, with the Washington Capitals doing the same with fellow backstop Remi Poirier. Soderblom entered the 2026-27 season set to be the backup to Spencer Knight once again. However, while the Blackhawks have struggled as a whole, Soderblom’s play has been anything but up to par. In five appearances so far, four starts, the 27-year-old has allowed 21 goals, giving him a 4.67 goals-against average and a .842 save percentage, along with a 0-3-1 record. Who the Hawks would call up to take his place is yet to be determined. Drew Commesso has been with the organization the longest, having played a couple of games with Chicago on top of his time with the AHL’s Rockford IceHogs, but Stanislav Berezhnoy has had better numbers early on this year with Rockford. In 117 NHL games, Soderblom has a record of 25-68-15, with a 3.65 GAA, a .885 SV% and one shutout. He’s in the final season of his two-year contract extension, which he signed in July 2025. The deal carries an AAV of $2.75 million. Poirier was acquired by the Capitals last Sunday in exchange for a seventh-round pick from the New Jersey Devils , as the Devils had to make some roster moves after receiving Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets . Poirier, who was claimed off waivers by the Devils from the Dallas Stars , has yet to play a game this season. He has spent the past three seasons with the Stars’ top farm team, the Texas Stars. In 137 regular-season games in the AHL, the 25-year-old is 70-51-16, with a 2.76 GAA, a .908 SV% and six shutouts. items.summary: The Chicago Blackhawks have had a calamitous start to the 2026-27 season, losing 14 of their first 18 games. They hit a new nadir Saturday in a devastating beatdown by the Carolina Hurricanes, and there's no light at the end of the tunnel for this Hawks team. And that fact isn't likely to change.
items.body: James Guillory-Imagn Images James Guillory-Imagn Images How The Chicago Blackhawks Are Experiencing The Worst-Case Scenario Adam Proteau Partner Nov 8, 2026 7:47 PM Published Nov 8, 2026 7:47 PM The Chicago Blackhawks have had a calamitous start to the 2026-27 season, losing 14 of their first 18 games. They hit a new nadir Saturday in a devastating beatdown by the Carolina Hurricanes, and there's no light at the end of the tunnel for this Hawks team. And that fact isn't likely to change. The Chicago Blackhawks came into this season with one base-level goal: to be competitive in a way the franchise simply hasn’t been since 2019-20 – the last season they made it to the Stanley Cup playoffs. The Blackhawks were always going to be up against it making the post-season in the Central Division, but they needed to at least show a modicum of improvement to demonstrate they were on the right track back to relevance. Unfortunately, the Hawks have come out of the gate losing 14 of 18 games – including 13 in regulation. Chicago is the NHL's second-worst team, and they’re well on their way to finishing in eighth place in the Central for the fifth consecutive season. More Videos They hit a new low on Saturday, getting dismantled by the Carolina Hurricanes in a 9-2 embarrassment. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Wendell Cruz The NHL’s Department of Player Safety announced Sunday that New York Islanders defenseman Logan Stanley has been fined $3,865 for slashing New Jersey Devils forward Nico Hischier. In 10 NHL seasons, the New Jersey captain has 206 goals and 293 assists for 499 points in 626 career regular-season games. Forward Bo Horvat and defenseman Matthew Schaefer are tied for the team lead with 16 points; Horvat has a team-leading seven goals while Schaefer has 11 assists. items.body: Logan Stanley is facing some discipline after a net-front tussle. The New York Islanders defenceman has been fined $3,865.98, the maximum amount allowable under the collective bargaining agreement, for slashing New Jersey Devils forward Nico Hischier , the NHL's department of player safety announced Sunday. The incident occurred in the second period of Saturday's 5-4 Devils overtime win. Near the end of the frame, Stanley laid into the net-front Hischier, forcing the Devils captain onto the ice. As Hischier got up, he poked at Stanley, to which the Islanders defenceman retaliated with a hard slash, sending Hischier to the ice once more, then pushed him while he was already down. The two players then exchanged some words and a scrum ensued after play was called dead. Stanley received two minor penalties on the play — one for the slash and another for roughing as part of the scrum. The 28-year-old Kitchener, Ont., native leads the Islanders in penalty minutes with 34 in his first year with the team. He also had five assists in 16 games.

items.summary: The Washington Capitals’ Tom Wilson won’t face further discipline after his actions on Saturday night.
items.body: The Washington Capitals ' Tom Wilson won't face further discipline after his actions on Saturday. Wilson delivered a hard hit to the back of Florida Panthers ' Sandis Vilmanis in the first period that sent the forward headfirst into the area where the glass meets the boards. Vilmanis left the game and did not return, and Wilson received a major penalty for boarding and a game misconduct for the play. After speculation about whether Wilson would face a hearing for the hit, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Sunday that he's hearing the Capitals' star will not face supplemental discipline. Panthers coach Paul Maurice said after the game that Florida was waiting on more information about Vilmanis' condition. “Getting looked at by another doctor tomorrow," he said. "But probably we’ll have to wait until we get him back to see our guys before we have a real good idea, get some imaging.” Wilson has been suspended several times during his 14-year career. He was given 20 games for a blindside hit to the head in 2018, a ban later reduced to 14 games on appeal after he had already served 16. He received a seven-game suspension for boarding Boston’s Brandon Carlo with head contact in 2021 and six games in 2024 for a stick to the face of Toronto Maple Leafs forward Noah Gregor. The 22-year-old Vilmanis had his first career two-goal game Wednesday night when Florida beat Chicago.

items.summary: Defenceman Kevin Bahl is set to undergo season-ending surgery to repair a ruptured Achilles tendon, the team announced Sunday.
items.body: The Calgary Flames have lost a piece on their blue line for the remainder of the year. Defenceman Kevin Bahl is set to undergo season-ending surgery to repair a ruptured Achilles tendon, the team announced Sunday. "A terrible break for a guy that I would consider our best player up to this point in the season," head coach Ryan Huska said of Bahl's injury. "Unfortunately, sometimes things happen, and because of that, we're losing a really good player for the rest of the year." Bahl suffered the injury on Friday prior to warmups ahead of the game against the Anaheim Ducks and was promptly ruled out. Joel Hanley entered the lineup in his place. The 26-year-old had played in all 16 of Calgary's games this season, averaging 21:56 of ice time per night while collecting one goal and one assist. Playing in his seventh NHL season, the New Westminster, B.C., native has picked up 12 goals and 53 assists in 313 games split between the Flames and New Jersey Devils. Bahl was acquired by the Flames in 2024 as part of the trade that sent Jacob Markstrom to New Jersey.

items.title: Sunday Overreactions: Will Blackhawks’ rebuild ever turn a corner?
items.summary: The Blackhawks have missed the playoffs six years in a row and appear headed for a seventh. Has their rebuild hit a wall? Michael Amato discusses that and more in Sunday Overreactions.
items.body: It’s early November and the Chicago Blackhawks are in a familiar spot. Second-to-last in the NHL, with a league-worst minus-37 goal differential and barreling through another season that feels destined to be lost. The pain of a rebuild is usually a small price to pay for three Stanley Cups from Chicago’s previous core, but this one has been particularly agonizing. The Blackhawks have missed the playoffs six years in a row and appear headed for a seventh. There also doesn’t seem to be many positive signs to build on going forward. Sure, Connor Bedard looks every bit of a superstar in the making, though there aren’t many running mates who are going to help the Blackhawks captain imminently. Rebuilds take time, but it’s important that an organization is moving in the right direction and there’s a light at the end of the tunnel. I’m not sure anyone can say that about Chicago right now. This is Bedard’s fourth season and the team has never finished any higher than 31st since he joined the NHL. Where are the Blackhawks right now in the standings? You guessed it, 31st. Bedard needs more help. Theoretically, that help should be coming, considering all the high draft picks Chicago has had in recent years. The Blackhawks picked in the first round 11 times between 2022-2025, which included a first overall (Bedard), second overall (Artyom Levshunov), third overall (Anton Frondell) and seventh overall (Kevin Korchinski). items.title: Canucks match effort by high-powered Oilers but crumble in third period
items.summary: It was a distinctly better effort than the Canucks managed in Thursday’s lifeless loss. But their opponent was much better too.
items.body: EDMONTON — When you are playing hockey until nearly midnight, typically you either have the cheaper ice time in your beer league or are playing in overtime in the Stanley Cup Playoffs. The Vancouver Canucks and Edmonton Oilers were doing neither on Saturday night. It was merely Game 19 for the Canucks, who at least for a while played playoff-like hockey even though they are the National Hockey League team most likely to be the first one eliminated from playoff contention this season. The Canucks competed admirably against the Oilers, a legitimate Stanley Cup contender, but surrendered two goals in three minutes early in the third period and lost the late-night game 4-2. It was a distinctly better effort than the Canucks managed in Thursday’s lifeless 6-2 loss to the Winnipeg Jets. But their opponent was much better, too. “A lot of, really, positives coming out of it, especially the first two periods, in terms of just the overall effort,” Vancouver coach Manny Malhotra said. “The attention to detail was there and because of that, we were in a situation going into third where we had an opportunity to win. “Again, it comes down to just those momentary lapses in detail and small missed assignments or a missed puck battle. Those are the things that add up. And eventually, obviously, against a team as high-powered as Edmonton, when you give them those little looks, they're going to make good on them.” Oiler Jason Dickinson scored on his second rebound chance to break a 1-1 tie 49 seconds into the third period, and Connor McDavid saucered a backdoor pass for Leon Draisaitl to one-time for a power-play goal 3:11 later. (It’s) a very tight-knit group. It’s been a tough start. Obviously it’s not what we expected. Every guy knows that we’ve got a little more.” The Blackhawks trailed 7-0 through two periods before Roman Kantserov and Bedard scored in the third period. “It’s a hard pill to swallow. At the end of the day we got our butts kicked,” Chicago coach Jeff Blashill said. “We’ve got to make this kind of a bottom point in the year. We have to find a way to claw our way out of this.” The Blackhawks have lost six straight (0-5-1) and nine of their past 10 (1-8-1). They are 4-13-1, last in the Central Division. Only the Vancouver Canucks (3-15-1, seven points) have fewer points than Chicago’s nine. "There's frustration,” Bedard said. “When you're waking up and going to bed, you're thinking about the record. But at the end of the day, we've got to be better.” Bedard missed Chicago’s first six games before making his season debut on Oct. 13. items.title: Penguins’ Sidney Crosby moves to sixth all-time in NHL scoring
items.summary: Crosby recorded his 1,772nd career point and passed Marcel Dionne for sixth on the NHL’s all-time list.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sidney Crosby moved into sole possession of sixth place on the NHL’s all-time points list after he scored twice to help the Pittsburgh Penguins win 5-2 over the Los Angeles Kings Saturday night. Crosby passed Hockey Hall of Famer Marcel Dionne with his 1,772nd point after he deflected the puck past Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper in the second period. He scored an empty netter to seal the win for Pittsburgh. The 39-year-old now has six goals and six assists for 12 points in 17 games this season. In 2025-26, Crosby passed Mario Lemieux and Steve Yzerman for eighth and seventh all-time in points, respectively. He now needs 26 points to pass Hall of Famer Ron Francis for fifth on the all-time list. Across 21 NHL seasons, Crosby has 660 goals and 1,113 assists for 1,773 points in 1,437 career regular-season games. He has hit the 100-point mark in six seasons and recorded at least 50 assists in a season 12 times. During that time, he’s broken the 100-point mark six times, recorded at least 50 assists 12 times, hit the 30-goal mark 13 times and has averaged more than a point-per-game in every season of his career. Crosby also has 72 goals and 134 assists for 206 points in 186 career playoff games. He captained the Penguins to three Stanley Cup championships in 2009, 2016 and 2017, and helped them reach the Stanley Cup Final in 2008. He also won the Conn Smythe Trophy in both 2016 and 2017. Crosby has twice won each of the Hart Trophy, the Art Ross Trophy, the Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophy and the Ted Lindsay Award.

items.body: EDMONTON -- Ryan Nugent-Hopkins sustained an apparent head injury 45 seconds into the second period of a 4-2 win for the Edmonton Oilers against the Vancouver Canucks at Rogers Place on Saturday and did not return to the game. The forward was hit on the side of the head with an attempted shoot-in by Oilers defenseman Ryan Shea. Nugent-Hopkins left the ice immediately and did not return. “I don’t think he is (going to miss much time), actually,” Edmonton coach Mike Babcock said after the game. “Initially, you’re worried about a broken jaw and they did an assessment on that. Just knowing our medical guys, there will probably be more assessments tomorrow. But I just shook his hand, he was in the hallway and seemed to be doing OK.” The 33-year-old has 11 points (four goals, seven assists) in nine games. He missed the first nine games of the season with a lower-body injury and made his season debut in a 6-5 shootout win against the Carolina Hurricanes on Oct. 22. Nugent-Hopkins broke the Oilers all-time games played record in a 4-3 shootout loss at the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday, playing in his 1,038th game. Selected by Edmonton with the No. 1 pick in the 2011 NHL Draft, Nugent-Hopkins is in his 16th season and has 815 points (295 goals, 520 assists) in 1,040 games.

items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google Two of the NHL’s best young defensemen showed off a different side of their games on Saturday night. Rather than creating offense, Matthew Schaefer and Luke Hughes exchanged punches late in the second period of their heated Metropolitan Division rivalry matchup between the New York Islanders and New Jersey Devils . The two were the main event of a fracas that saw five separate roughing penalties called as tempers flared around New York’s net. The conflict started in front of the Islanders’ net after Logan Stanley slashed Devils forward Nico Hischier and tussled with defenseman Brett Pesce . Attention then turned behind the net, where Schaefer and Hughes turned up the temperature to 11 as they threw gloved haymakers at each other’s faces, and Schaefer ended up on top of Hughes in a pile-up. “I don’t know,” Hughes said . “He just had my visor, and we just started…it doesn’t really matter. I think hockey is an emotional sport, and I wouldn’t call that a fight at all. Neither of us had our gloves off. It’s part of the game, two competitive guys.” Schaefer, who scored his fifth goal of the season in the game, shared a very similar take on the play. “I don’t know,” Schaefer said . “I think it was just kind of roughing up a bit. Just kind of grabbing each other.” The heated disagreement is very out of character for both players, as neither the 19-year-old Schaefer nor the 23-year-old Hughes has ever gotten into an NHL fight. Schaefer maxed out at 38 penalty minutes in his rookie 2025-26 campaign, while Hughes has never recorded more than 32 penalty minutes in a season during his parts of five years with the Devils. items.body: LOS ANGELES — Sidney Crosby scored two goals while moving into sole possession of sixth place on the NHL’s career scoring list, and the Pittsburgh Penguins snapped their four-game skid with a 5-2 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday night. The 39-year-old Crosby broke his tie with Kings great Marcel Dionne by scoring his 1,772nd point when Evgeni Malkin’s one-timer deflected in off him in the second period. Crosby added a late empty-net goal, diving face-first on the ice to tip it home. Tommy Novak got two goals in the first six minutes and Egor Chinakhov also scored for the Penguins, who moved Crosby and the 40-year-old Malkin onto their top line before the game in an effort to spark their struggling lineup. Sergei Murashov made 26 saves as Pittsburgh opened a three-game California trip with just its third win in 11 games. Corey Perry and Alex Laferriere scored and Darcy Kuemper stopped only 14 shots for the Kings, who have lost two of the last three during their seven-game homestand. Novak put the Pens ahead less than two minutes after the opening faceoff after controlling a rebound in front. Less than 3 1/2 minutes later, he carried the puck into the zone and followed behind Ben Kindel to cash in another rebound for his seventh career multi-goal game. Perry scored midway through the first when Mikey Anderson's high shot off the end boards ricocheted down toward the crease, where he slapped it out of mid-air for the second goal of his 22nd NHL season. Chinakhov scored on a power play late in the first to put the Penguins up 3-1, but Laferriere scored on a power play early in the second. items.summary: Jacob Fowler showed the calm and poise of freshly enshrined Hall of Famer Carey Price on Saturday, helping Montreal beat the Maple Leafs. As Eric Engels writes, it said everything you need to know about the Canadiens’ young netminder.
items.body: If not when the Montreal Canadiens allowed two goals in less than a minute to turn a 3-0 lead into sudden hope for the Toronto Maple Leafs, then certainly as the game was winding down while both Alex Newhook and Kirby Dach were defending a Leafs six-on-four advantage without sticks in their hands. But this week didn’t end how it started for the Canadiens, much to Jacob Fowler ’s delight. He was the one guy who didn’t get first crack at redemption against the Utah Mammoth Thursday, two nights after the Canadiens allowed the Winnipeg Jets to make NHL history by completing the latest four-goal comeback ever in a game—in the final 2:39 of regulation—before allowing them to win it with 1:30 to go in overtime. Fowler made 36 saves before five Jets shots found the back of his net, and then he had to sit with that awful feeling until the start of Saturday’s game in Toronto. To think it might be coming back up towards the end of the night, like a bad case of acid reflux, as momentum quickly shifted the Leafs’ way… But no, the 21-year-old swallowed hard and reset himself—and the Canadiens. After they won 4-2, Newhook, who scored the first two goals, confirmed to Sportsnet’s Kyle Bukauskas that Fowler came over to the bench and reassured the team. “It was good to see,” Newhook said. “He’s got a good presence back there. He’s got a calming presence for sure. For a young guy to be able to step up like that and come to the bench, he’s not panicking and we know he’s gonna be on it behind us, so it’s good. I liked hearing it.” Seeing it on Hall of Fame weekend, with freshly enshrined Canadiens legend Carey Price looking on, added weight to Fowler’s performance. This was already a heavy situation. Can I offer you an apple in this trying time? 🍏 📺: @Sportsnet or stream on Sportsnet+ ➡️ https://t.co/qAjIlD26Mn pic.twitter.com/UFu7ltqXq8 The broadcast team of Chris Cuthbert and Craig Simpson had a good laugh at the odd moment, pointing out that Fowler is apple-less (zero assists) for his NHL career (27 games) so far. No, no, this apple appears more to be one of those soft squeezable ones that you'd get as some kind of giveaway at a corporate retreat or to keep your arm active when donating blood. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Los Angeles’ Alex Laferriere preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to the goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 4:29 (15:31 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.title: Oilers’ Connor McDavid ties Adam Oates with assists in 18 consecutive games
items.body: Connor McDavid is taking a real run at one of Wayne Gretzky's records. The Edmonton Oilers star notched an assist in his 18th consecutive game to start the season on Saturday. McDavid set up Mattias Ekholm for the first goal of the night in the first period against the visiting Vancouver Canucks. McDavid moved into a tie with Adam Oates (1992-93, Boston Bruins) for second on the NHL list of most consecutive games with an assist. Another Hall of Famer, Gretzky, owns the record with 23 games in a row with an assist, set in 1990-91 with the Oilers. If McDavid can keep his run going, he'd be able to tie and break the record in Florida and Tampa Bay on Nov. 17 and 19. McDavid entered the night with a league-leading 44 points, 13 ahead of teammate Leon Draisaitl in the NHL scoring race.

items.title: McDavid extends assist streak, Oilers double up slumping Canucks
items.body: EDMONTON — Leon Draisaitl had two goals and an assist and Connor McDavid added three assists as the Edmonton Oilers came away with a 4-2 victory over the struggling Vancouver Canucks on Saturday. Mattias Ekholm and Jason Dickinson also scored for the Oilers (12-3-3) who snapped a two-game losing skid. The Oilers are 10-0-2 when they score first this season. Devon Levi returned from injury to record 20 saves and improve to 7-1-0 in the Edmonton net. Max Sasson and Brock Boeser replied for the Canucks (3-15-1) who have lost five straight and 15 of their last 16. Canucks: Swedish forward Liam Öhgren was unable to extend his scoring streak to three games. The 22-year-old had scored four goals in his previous five games, including his first-ever power-play goal. Oilers: McDavid extended his season-starting points and assists streak to 18 games. He now leads the league with 10 goals, 37 assists and 47 points. The Oilers captain matched Adam Oates for the second-longest assist streak in NHL history behind only Wayne Gretzky’s 23 games set in 1990-91. McDavid also became the sixth player in NHL history with a season-opening 18-game point streak. Edmonton took a 3-1 lead four minutes into the final frame as their potent power play struck when McDavid sent it across to Draisaitl and he unleashed his patented one-timer for his 15th of the season. Evan Bouchard extended his points streak to six games and both he and Draisaitl have points in 16 of 18 games. The Canucks came into the game sporting a dreadful minus-30 goal differential, a staggering 4.61 goals against per game. Meanwhile, the Oilers came in as the league’s highest-scoring team, averaging 4.12 goals per contest.

items.title: Jack Hughes scores in overtime as Devils rally past Islanders
items.body: NEW YORK — Jack Hughes scored in overtime to lift the New Jersey Devils to a 5-4 victory over the New York Islanders on Saturday. Dougie Hamilton, Luke Evangelista, Declan Chisholm and Evan Rodrigues also scored for New Jersey, which extended its winning streak to four games. Jake Allen made 19 saves. Hughes scored with 3:42 remaining in overtime, keeping the puck on a two-on-one rush before firing a shot past Ilya Sorokin’s blocker. Anthony Duclair, Matthew Schaefer, Simon Holmstrom and Victor Eklund scored for New York, which lost its third straight game. Sorokin finished with 45 saves and captain Bo Horvat added two assists. The Devils erased a two-goal deficit in the third period, capped by Hamilton’s power-play goal with 6:18 remaining in regulation. Jack Hughes curled around the net before finding Hamilton in the slot for the tying goal. Evangelista started the comeback when he pulled New Jersey within a goal at 6:08 of the third period. The Islanders took a 2-1 lead after the first period. Duclair opened the scoring with less than five minutes remaining, Rodrigues tied it 17 seconds later and Schaefer put New York back ahead with his fifth goal of the season. Chisholm tied the score at 2 just 4:42 into the second period when Jesper Bratt fired a shot off the end boards that took an awkward bounce around the net, allowing Chisholm to bury the rebound. Two of Islanders goaltender Ilya Sorokin’s best saves came against Devils captain Nico Hischier. Sorokin denied Hischier on a breakaway in the closing seconds of the second period and stopped a one-timer in the opening minute of the third.

items.title: Ref appears to offer Canadiens’ Fowler an apple
items.summary: An apple nearly took a bite out of Montreal Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler on Saturday.
items.body: An apple nearly took a bite out of Montreal Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler on Saturday. The apple found its way to the ice during the second period of a game between the Canadiens and Maple Leafs in Toronto. Referee TJ Luxmore was seen on camera holding it up to Fowler before disposing of it. Fowler told Sportsnet's Kyle Bukauskas after the game that the apple wasn't real but added that it was still one of the weirdest things he'd ever seen hit the ice. "I was pretty dialled in but I saw an apple come on the ice right in front of me. I'm used to tracking a black puck not a green apple," Fowler said with a laugh. "I saw that one and (Luxmore) told me he would have blown the play dead if they had gotten in the zone so thankfully they didn't get one there." The flying apple didn't faze Fowler, who stopped 26 saves in a 4-2 win.

items.title: USA beats Czechia to win gold at 2026 U-17 World Challenge
items.summary: The Americans have now moved into second place all time with seven gold medals.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis The United States have returned to the top of the World U-17 Challenge podium again, beating Czechia 3-0 in Oakville to win gold. The Americans have now moved into second place all time with seven gold medals, with Canada Ontario (a defunct squad) leading the way at eight. USA has won a tournament-leading 19 medals at the tournament, while Czechia has taken its second silver medal. USA’s victory officially ended Canada’s three-year gold-medal streak dating back to 2023. The win also marked the Americans’ third gold medal over the past decade. Carter Morris scored the lone goal in the first period, with Dean Stevens and Joey Cullen snagging assists. Morris then scored again at 12:15 in the third period, capitalizing on the power play after Cullen found him in a scoring position. Cameron Evans then scored an empty-netter with 12.8 seconds left to seal the deal, while Mason Martin stopped all 29 shots sent his way. Matyas Novotny had another strong effort for the Czechs, making multiple high-quality saves throughout the the third period. In the end, USA – who plays together throughout the year as part of the USA Hockey National Team Development Program – had the edge in chemistry. Canada Red beat Canada White 8-4 for bronze earlier in the day, while Sweden stomped Finland 8-5 in the fifth-place affair. Maddox Schultz led the way with six goals and 16 points in five games, marking the fourth-best output in a single tournament. The netminder has been recalled as a non-roster, emergency third-string option as Seattle prepares for two games against the Carolina Hurricanes. Both games will take place at Veikkaus Arena in Helsinki, roughly a seven hour drive south of Kokko’s hometown of Oulu. He played much of his junior and early pro career close to Oulu. Kokko has served as the starter for the AHL’s Coachella Valley Firebirds to start the season. He has set a 4-3-3 record and .893 save percentage through 10 games so far. While a meager stat-line, Kokko has outperformed backup Victor Ostman , who has a 1-2-1 record and .872 save percentage through four games. Kokko has served as Coachella Valley’s starter through the last two seasons, combining for a 39-20-4 record and .907 save percentage through 68 games. He has also made four appearances in the NHL, marked by a 1-2-0 record and .875 save percentage. The Finnish goaltender will only be available if both Joey Daccord and Philipp Grubauer become unavailable during the back-to-back games. If not, he’ll enjoy a trip with Finnish compatriots Kaapo Kakko and Jani Nyman .

items.title: Agent for Blackhawks’ Byram explains absence
items.body: After missing the past nine games with an undisclosed upper-body injury, Byram's agent is attempting to provide a bit of clarity on the situation. "Darren Ferris reached out to me today," Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman said on Saturday Headlines. "He wanted to say that the reason Byram has not come back yet is due to his desire to have Byram see a certain specialist." Ferris did not elaborate on what Byram's injury is or what the specialist would look at. "He just said that he wants Byram to see a certain specialist and until that gets done, that's the reason Byram has not returned," Friedman continued. Byram last played on Oct. 13 and did not appear to have an injury. Two days later, head coach Jeff Blashill classified the defenceman as day-to-day with an upper-body injury. The Cranbrook, B.C. native was the marquee addition for the Blackhawks this off-season, trading the 2026 fourth-overall pick to the Buffalo Sabres in exchange for the blue-liner. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Toronto Maple Leafs announced on social media that defenseman Morgan Rielly left Saturday’s game against the Montreal Canadiens with a lower-body injury and would not return. It’s not clear how or when Rielly sustained the injury, but he left the bench during the first period. He finished the night with 5:45 of ice time on eight shifts. Now in his 14th NHL season, Rielly had 98 goals and 463 assists for 561 points in 968 career regular-season games. Since entering the league in 2013-14, Rielly has recorded three 50-assist seasons and has four seasons where he recorded at least 50 points. His best season came in 2018-19 when he posted 20 goals and 52 assists for 72 points. That season, he finished fifth in Norris Trophy voting and fourth in the Lady Byng Trophy vote. Rielly, a native of Vancouver, also has 15 goals and 32 assists for 47 points in 70 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. Taken No. 5 overall by the Leafs in the 2012 NHL Entry Draft, Rielly spent parts of three seasons in the Western Hockey League with the Moose Jaw Warriors. He finished with 21 goals and 79 assists for 100 points in 143 career regular-season games. He also had nine assists in 11 WHL playoff games. Internationally, Rielly represented Canada at the World Championships multiple times and helped them win a gold medal in 2016. He was also part of the 2013 World Junior Championship roster.

items.title: ‘Extremely grateful’: Price, Bergeron headline 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame class
items.body: TORONTO — Carey Price spent a lot of his youth on the road and in the air. Growing up in a remote part of British Columbia, that's what chasing his hockey dream required. When the phone rang in June to announce he would be joining the game's greats, Price was fittingly in a familiar situation — driving. "I was on my way to go visit my grandmother at the hospital," recalled the former Montreal Canadiens goaltender. "Hockey Hall of Fame came up with my caller ID in my truck, so pretty excited about that. Got to spend the rest of the day with my grandmother, who made a recovery. Price had plenty of those in the NHL and with Canada on the international stage. Now he will share another one Monday with the rest of the hall's 2026 class. The netminder headlines this year's inductees alongside Patrice Bergeron, Pekka Rinne, Keith Tkachuk and Cindy Curley in the player category set to be enshrined Monday. Brian Burke will go in as a builder. "A long road to get to this point," Price, who starred in Montreal for all 15 of his NHL seasons and will enter the hall in his second year of eligibility, said Saturday. "I'm just extremely thankful for that journey and everything that I learned along the way — not only in hockey but in life." The No. 5 pick at the 2005 draft, Price won the Hart Trophy as league MVP and the Vezina Trophy as its top goaltender in 2015. The 39-year-old from Anahim Lake, B.C., finished with a 361-261-79 record, .917 save percentage, 2.51 goals-against average and 49 shutouts across 712 regular-season games in a career that was, at times, hampered by injury. Price had even better big-moment numbers before a knee issue forced him to stop playing beyond the 2021-22 campaign. items.title: Jets’ Josh Morrissey sheds non-contact jersey at practice
items.body: The Winnipeg Jets appear to be getting their No. 1 defenceman back soon. Josh Morrissey shed his non-contact jersey and was a full participant in practice on Saturday for the first time since going down with a wrist injury in early October. Morrissey didn't speak to the media after the skate but head coach Scott Arniel said, "He’s getting closer." “That was the first time that we really got him ramped up," Arniel added without committing to Morrissey playing Sunday against the Lightning. "I’m not hiding anything. We’ve still got to get to see how this went after today’s practice. That decision won’t get made (yet). That full lineup won’t be (known) until (Sunday)." The Jets have missed Morrissey in the lineup and sit seventh in the Central Division with a 6-8-3 record. items.title: Heir Canada: Is Jet Greaves The Next Goaltender To Take The Reins For Team Canada?
items.summary: Jet Greaves suddenly seems like a prime candidate to ascend to the blue-paint throne for his home nation. And now that he is armed with some financial security and the starting gig in the Columbus net, he’s truly cleared for his NHL takeoff.
items.body: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Heir Canada: Is Jet Greaves The Next Goaltender To Take The Reins For Team Canada? Carol Schram Partner Nov 7, 2026 8:19 PM Published Nov 7, 2026 8:19 PM Jet Greaves suddenly seems like a prime candidate to ascend to the blue-paint throne for his home nation. And now that he is armed with some financial security and the starting gig in the Columbus net, he’s truly cleared for his NHL takeoff. When international best-on-best hockey returned at the 4 Nations Face-Off and the Milan Olympics, fans in the Great White North came face-to-face with the stark realization that Hockey Canada didn’t have a superstar netminder who could uphold the elite standards set by past Olympic gold medallists Carey Price, Roberto Luongo or Martin Brodeur. Could the nation’s hopes for the 2028 World Cup of Hockey and even the 2030 Olympics therefore rest on the shoulders of an undrafted late-bloomer who checks in at just six-foot and 190 pounds? Jet Greaves made his full-time NHL debut last season at 24, then made a strong case for himself in his first national-team showing at May’s World Championship in Switzerland. Over eight games, he allowed just 15 goals and recorded a .920 save percentage. “When you’re growing up playing hockey in Canada, one of your biggest dreams is to wear the Maple Leaf on your chest,” he said. “To be able to do that for the first time was super special.” More Videos The World Championship followed Greaves’ stellar campaign with the Columbus Blue Jackets , where he established himself as his team’s No. 1 with a record of 26-19-9 to go along with a 2.60 goals-against average and .908 SP. He also had some of the best advanced stats in the league, including the ninth-best goals saved above expected, per moneypuck.com .

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Well, it’s been a while since we’ve had to write something like this. During a matchup between the Washington Capitals and Florida Panthers on Saturday afternoon, Capitals forward Tom Wilson was ejected after boarding Panthers defenseman Sandis Vilmanis. The incident came a little before the halfway mark of the opening period in the U.S. capital. As Vilmanis was trying to move the puck out of the Florida zone, Wilson came from his side, but ended up drilling the Latvian blueliner into the sideboards from behind. Vilmanis went down to the Panthers’ dressing room following the hit. Wilson was given a five-minute major for boarding and a game misconduct. While it’s too early to tell whether his actions will result in any additional consequences, Wilson is far from unfamiliar with supplemental discipline. The 32-year-old has been suspended six times by the NHL Department of Player Safety, including three times during the 2017-18 season, and fined on five other occasions. Wilson has tried to keep his nose clean lately, as he hasn’t been fined or suspended since April 2025. The Toronto native earned a reputation for being a dirty player, but as he has grown older, he has tried to mold his game into more of an effective power forward, rather than a brute force. Yet, he’s registered at least 100 points in each of the past three seasons, though he hasn’t come close to challenging his career-high 187 points, which came during that 2017-18 campaign. In 14 games with Washington so far this season, Wilson has scored two goals and three assists for five points. His 45 penalty minutes put him second in the NHL behind Boston Bruins defender Nikita Zadorov.

items.body: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Did Oilers' McDavid Overreact To Helleson And Ducks Incident? But is McDavid's response a bit of an overreaction? For the most part, in his Hockey Hall of Fame-level career, Edmonton Oilers superstar center Connor McDavid has been a cool, calm, unflappable icon. So it’s rare to see him get angry – at least, not outside of the Oilers’ dressing room. So it was a little out of character to see McDavid going off on Anaheim Ducks defenseman Drew Helleson after he drove McDavid into the Ducks’ net. McDavid stayed down on the ice briefly, and when he got up, it was clear that he was upset with Helleson. And his post-game comments confirmed it. items.title: Quick Shifts: Vinni Lettieri is fighting to survive in the NHL
items.summary: With the Maple Leafs returning to health, Vinni Lettieri is literally fighting to keep his spot in the lineup. Whatever it takes. Luke Fox digs into his battle and 11 more observations from around in the NHL in this edition of Quick Shifts.
items.body: A quick mix of the things we gleaned from the week of hockey, serious and less so, and rolling four lines deep. I don’t need to crash into you to drink your wine. 1. In the NHL, one man’s return to health always spells bad news for one of his teammates. And so, while the Toronto Maple Leafs get a nice boost with John Tavares jumping into their lineup this weekend, Vinni Lettieri quietly slides to the outside. The 31-year-old journeyman is literally fighting to stick in the show. Lettieri is undrafted, he’s five-foot-10, and he’s changed teams five times, never making more than six figures. Last season, he never got called up. Spent the whole winter on the farm. So, when the Minnesota native got off to a hot start with the Marlies and was promoted to the Leafs in the wake of injuries, he dropped the mitts twice in four days, taking on Connor Murphy in Edmonton and Cale Fleury in Seattle. “My last NHL fight was Scott Laugton in pre-season when I was with the New York Rangers nine years ago,” Lettieri says. “With those two fights, I've had three in my whole career.” Lettieri scored once in his eight-game look and outlasted Bo Groulx, who was waived down. items.summary: Following a ruling last week from the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) to reinstate Russia to international hockey competitions, the IIHF stated on Saturday that, while it disagrees with the ruling, it is taking the steps required by the CAS’s decision regarding possible reimplementation.
items.body: The IIHF has come to a decision regarding Russian and Belarusian participation in upcoming tournaments. Following a ruling last week from the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) to reinstate Russia to international hockey competitions, the IIHF stated on Saturday that, while it disagrees with the ruling, it is taking the steps required by the CAS's decision regarding possible reimplementation. "While the IIHF continues to disagree with the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport concerning Russian participation in IIHF Championships, we are taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization's financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey," the IIHF said in its statement. "The IIHF must work within the applicable framework while upholding its responsibility to preserve international competition and protect the sport as a whole. "The IIHF is therefore exploring all available avenues, including opening discussions with all affected MNAs (Member National Associations), including the Russian Ice Hockey Federation, to identify a constructive way forward that serves the interests of global ice hockey." Last week on Friday, the CAS overturned an exclusion of Russian participation in international ice hockey tournaments, put in place since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The IIHF has opposed Russia's immediate reinstatement, citing security, logistical and competitive concerns, while several European hockey federations have said their teams would refuse to face Russia. Since the Court of Arbitration for Sport's (CAS) decision to reinstate Russia to participate in international hockey competitions, several other countries have threatened to boycott IIHF tournaments. Even Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he would not allow the Russian U-20 World Junior Championship team to participate in the tournament taking place in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta., this winter. The IIHF has come out with a statement on Saturday regarding CAS's decision and the participation of Russia and Belarus in their competitions. More Videos "In accordance with the principles approved by the 2022 IIHF Semi-Annual Congress, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) Council has decided that Belarusian U20 and senior men’s national teams will not participate in the IIHF World Junior Championship 2027 and the IIHF World Championship 2027, respectively. "Separately, while the IIHF continues to disagree with the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) concerning Russian participation in IIHF Championships, we are taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization’s financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey." items.title: If you could take over as GM of any NHL team, whom would you pick?
items.summary: Factoring in roster, prospects, market and climate, here’s where we’d go.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Oct 17, 2026; Montreal, Quebec, CAN; Montreal Canadiens forward Cole Caufield (13) celebrates with teammates forward Juraj Slafkovsky (20) and forward Nick Suzuki (14) after scoring a goal against the Buffalo Sabres during the first period at the Bell Centre. Mandatory Credit: Eric Bolte-Imagn Images No two NHL teams’ futures are created the same. Some are set up to contend for years to come. Others find themselves in desperate win-now situations. Some are in scorched-earth rebuilds. It’s time to play a game. Look around at every team’s setup and consider the timeline, market and talent. You’re the hottest new GM candidate in the NHL. You’re allowed to take over one team. Which would you choose and why? MATT LARKIN: I was so close to picking the San Jose Sharks but, as an Ottawa-born Torontonian, I can’t bring myself to spend hockey season in a warm climate. I’ll take the New York Islanders job. I’m all-in on Matthew Schaefer having a Hall of Fame career. He’s my guy, the future captain I’ll build around, with up-and comers like Victor Eklund to complement him. I’ll be sure to hold onto Ilya Sorokin as my goalie, too. But I’m not convinced this team is ready to contend. I’ll sell off some veterans, such as Mathew Barzal, to obtain some additional first-round picks. I’ll go backward to go forward in hopes of crafting a higher-ceiling team that can return to its early-1980s glory. And the Tri-State Area is a fun place to live for a city boy like me. STEVEN ELLIS: Sign me up to run the San Jose Sharks . The idea of building a team around Macklin Celebrini has to excite any potential candidate, and that’s just scratching the surface.
